question: If the profit on selling an article for ₹986 is the same as the loss incurred on selling it for ₹726, then the cost price of the article is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If profit at one SP equals loss at another SP, then Cost Price = average of both SPs

CP = (986 + 726) ÷ 2

CP = 1712 ÷ 2

CP = 856

**∴ Answer = 856**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price 1 = 986 (profit), Selling Price 2 = 726 (loss)

**Formula used:**

Profit = SP − CP and Loss = CP − SP

**Calculation:**

⇒ Profit = 986 − CP

⇒ Loss = CP − 726

⇒ Given Profit = Loss

⇒ 986 − CP = CP − 726

⇒ 986 + 726 = 2CP

⇒ 1712 = 2CP

⇒ CP = 856

**∴ The correct answer is 856.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equal Profit & Loss Concept

When profit at one SP equals loss at another, CP is the average of the two SPs.

Profit Formula

Profit = SP − CP

Loss Formula

Loss = CP − SP
